observations: Two eye sockets are drawn as mismatched shapes — a square on the left crossed with orange diagonals, a circle on the right — both leaving white voids at their centers against a deep maroon ground.
A wide rectangular mouth sits low in the composition, filled with a row of blocky white teeth outlined in black, anchoring the lower third of the face.
Orange strokes radiate upward from between the eyes, while white, blue, and purple scribble lines loop freely across the entire surface, extending past the face into the dark border.
reading: The mismatched eye shapes — one squared, one round — give the face an off-balance stare that reads as wariness or challenge. Orange strokes above the brow push upward with force, while looping white and blue lines vibrate around the form rather than contain it. The blocky tooth-row below holds the composition in locked tension.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between titled neighbors #108 and #110. All three share a bared-teeth motif, but #109 replaces #108's bright multi-color ground with a concentrated maroon field, pulling the layered lines into tighter contrast.

connections.reason: Both works center a wide tooth-filled mouth low in the frame, but #108 spreads across a gray ground with a large heart shape dominating the upper face, while #109 replaces that motif with upward-radiating orange strokes on maroon.

Both #109 and #110 use a warm single-color ground — maroon versus burnt orange — but #110 dissolves the face into dense overlapping scribble, while #109 keeps the eye and mouth zones as distinct, readable shapes.

lookingQuestion: What does the difference in shape between the left and right eye — one squared with crossed diagonals, one a plain circle — do to your sense of where the face is looking?
ambiguities: The orange radiating strokes above the brow could be read as a crown, horns, or purely abstract mark-making; no supplied evidence resolves which reading was intended.
The nnotb #29 comparison image shows a full-body figure on a gray ground with a repeating rectangular border pattern — no strong formal link to #109 was found, so it was omitted.
